mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 z-score) in at least 70% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.10 z-score) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 0.3 percentage points for three consecutive months signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 z-score) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and the Consumer Price Index above their respective 12-month moving averages signals a dual shock of monetary tightening and inflation, which increases real discount rates and erodes real corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month moving averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 z-score) in at least 60% of co-triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in housing starts (HOUST) below the previous six-month average for four consecutive months indicates a contraction in the residential construction sector, which negatively impacts construction-related equities and drags on broader market returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.10 z-score) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent monthly contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for six consecutive months signals a broad-based slowdown in manufacturing activity, which reduces earnings expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for 6 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.10 z-score) in at least 60% of triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A concurrent rise in both payroll employment (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) over three months, despite the apparent contradiction, may indicate a shift in labor force participation or demographic effects; if such a pattern persists, it signals uncertainty and reduces investor confidence, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS rises while UNRATE rises for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.05 z-score) in at least 50% of co-triggered episodes.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals elevated precautionary savings and reduced marginal propensity to consume, which dampens demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 12-month moving average for 5 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative (< -0.10 z-score) in at least 50% of triggered episodes.
